args.title: plan-deviation-report.docx
args.body:
PLAN OF REORGANIZATION — DEVIATION REPORT
plan-deviation-report.docx
Matter: Bankruptcy Restructuring — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization
Practice Area: Bankruptcy Restructuring
Classification: Privileged and Confidential — Attorney Work Product

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This report compares the official committee’s redlined Plan of Reorganization (the “Committee Markup” or “Redline”) against the debtor’s original Plan of Reorganization (the “Debtor Plan” or “Base Plan”), reconciling the Redline against the valuation summary, the deal-team transmittal email, the disclosure statement excerpts, the disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the controlling client instruction in the latest partner correspondence.

The Committee Markup accepts most firm-standard and Debtor Plan provisions but introduces three material deviations:

1. Indemnification economics — silent reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible basket to a tipping basket.
2. Material Adverse Effect definition — new carve-outs for regulatory action of the precise type already at issue in this matter and disclosed on Schedule 3.7.
3. Survival / limitation period — a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations, contradicting the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Under the controlling client instruction (latest partner email), the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded and do not control. This report therefore recommends: (a) conditional acceptance of the tipping-basket conversion subject to protective conditions on the cap and on Schedule 5.2 retained-liability allocation; (b) rejection of the MAE regulatory carve-outs; and (c) rejection of the shortened survival period as a walk-away item.

II. SOURCE MATERIALS REVIEWED

A. Base / Debtor Materials
- Debtor’s original Plan of Reorganization and related firm-standard plan provisions (representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing/effectiveness, indemnification, termination, and survival).
- Disclosure statement excerpts describing plan treatment, residual risk allocation, and the factual predicate for the pending regulatory posture.
- Valuation summary supporting enterprise value, distributable value, and the economic assumptions underlying indemnification and residual liability capacity.

B. Committee / Counterparty Markup
- Committee redline of the Plan of Reorganization introducing the three deviations identified in Section III.

C. Schedules and Exhibits (controlling over general base-plan statements)
- Schedule 3.7 — discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the Markup’s Material Adverse Effect carve-outs.
- Schedule 5.2 — lists retained liabilities that the Markup’s indemnification changes would silently shift.
- Exhibit B — sets the survival matrix that the Markup’s limitation-period change contradicts.

D. Deal Correspondence (controlling instruction)
- Partner email thread. The latest message revises analysis priorities: the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages in the thread stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded; only the latest message controls.

III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS

DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion
(Basket: deductible → tipping; Cap: silently reduced)

Base Plan position
- Indemnification basket structured as a deductible (true deductible): losses below the basket threshold are borne by the indemnified party and do not count toward, and do not unlock, recovery above the threshold.
- Indemnification cap set at the negotiated baseline reflected in the Debtor Plan and consistent with residual value capacity indicated in the valuation summary.

Committee Markup position
- Converts the basket from a deductible basket to a tipping (first-dollar) basket, so that once losses exceed the threshold, the indemnifying party is responsible from the first dollar.
- Silently reduces the indemnification cap (no conspicuous call-out in the Redline narrative; change appears only in the operative dollar figure / cross-reference).

Interaction with schedules and valuation
- Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. The combination of a tipping basket and a reduced cap would silently shift economic exposure on those retained liabilities: tipping expands first-dollar reach once the threshold is crossed, while the reduced cap truncates upside recovery precisely where Schedule 5.2 residual items and plan-level indemnity are meant to backstop creditors and the reorganized debtor.
- The valuation summary’s residual-value and distributable-value assumptions are sensitive to uncapped or under-capped post-effective-date indemnity drag. A silent cap cut undermines the disclosure-statement description of residual risk and the feasibility narrative tied to those assumptions.

Client instruction and recommended disposition
- Basket conversion: CONCEDE (per controlling latest partner email), subject to the conditions below.
- Cap reduction: REJECT the silent reduction. Require restoration of the baseline cap (or an expressly negotiated and disclosed alternate cap) and conspicuous revision marks plus conforming disclosure-statement and valuation updates.
- Protective conditions if tipping basket is accepted:
  (i) restore or expressly re-strike the cap at not less than the Debtor Plan baseline;
  (ii) conform Schedule 5.2 and any plan supplement retained-liability schedule so that tipping does not reallocate Schedule 5.2 items by implication;
  (iii) add a short indemnification economics exhibit or plan supplement note reconciling basket type, threshold, cap, and Schedule 5.2 items to the valuation summary;
  (iv) require reciprocal clarity that the tipping mechanic does not expand indemnity for items expressly retained or non-indemnifiable under the confirmed plan.

Risk if unaddressed
- Creditors and the reorganized debtor absorb a hidden reduction in indemnity capacity; disclosure statement and confirmation record become inconsistent with operative plan economics; Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities migrate without bargained consideration.

DEVIATION 2 — Material Adverse Effect Definition — Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs

Base Plan position
- MAE definition follows firm-standard / Debtor Plan formulation without carve-outs that neutralize regulatory actions of the type already in view in this case.

Committee Markup position
- Adds carve-outs to the MAE definition for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter, narrowing the circumstances in which regulatory developments can constitute or contribute to an MAE (and thereby affecting conditionality, termination rights, and related plan-effectiveness or implementation protections keyed to MAE).

Interaction with schedules and disclosure
- Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these carve-outs. Because the scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials, the factual predicate for regulatory risk is already on the record. Carving that same risk out of MAE would allow the Committee to neutralize conditionality and walk-away/protection mechanics precisely where Schedule 3.7 has flagged live exposure.
- Disclosure statement excerpts that describe regulatory posture and residual risk would be misaligned if MAE no longer reaches the scheduled inquiries or closely related agency action.

Client instruction and recommended disposition
- REJECT the regulatory-action MAE carve-outs.
- Require either:
  (i) deletion of the new carve-outs and restoration of the Debtor Plan MAE definition; or
  (ii) if any regulatory qualifier is to remain, a narrow, expressly negotiated formulation that does not carve out the Schedule 3.7 inquiries or materially similar pending or threatened actions, with conforming disclosure-statement language.
- Cross-check all MAE-triggered conditions to effectiveness, implementation covenants, and termination/remedy provisions so that Schedule 3.7 risk remains actionable.

Risk if unaddressed
- MAE-based protections become illusory as to the principal known regulatory overhang; confirmation and effective-date conditionality weaken; Schedule 3.7 disclosure is converted from a risk allocator into a roadmap for stripping protections.

DEVIATION 3 — Survival / Limitation Period — Shortened Survival for Core Representations
(Walk-away issue under controlling client instruction)

Base Plan position
- Survival of core representations governed by the survival matrix in Exhibit B (and related plan/supplement references), preserving post-effective-date claim periods consistent with the negotiated risk allocation and the valuation summary’s treatment of contingent indemnity.

Committee Markup position
- Inserts a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations, contradicting Exhibit B’s survival matrix.

Interaction with schedules and exhibits
- Exhibit B controls the survival matrix. The Markup’s limitation-period change is in direct conflict with Exhibit B and would override it if the Redline were accepted without conforming exhibit amendments—an impermissible silent override of a controlling exhibit.
- Shortened survival compounds Deviation 1: even if basket/cap economics were repaired, a truncated survival window reduces the practical value of indemnity on core reps, including those tied to Schedule 5.2 retained-liability themes and regulatory matters adjacent to Schedule 3.7.

Client instruction and recommended disposition
- REJECT in full. Under the controlling latest partner email, any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue.
- Require restoration of Exhibit B survival periods for core representations with no abbreviated general limitation period that cuts across the matrix.
- If the Committee seeks a tailored outside date for discrete non-core items only, that must be negotiated expressly as an amendment to Exhibit B—not as a blanket limitation period—and remains subject to client re-approval because the standing instruction treats survival reduction as walk-away.

Risk if unaddressed
- Core rep indemnity becomes time-barred before residual risks mature; Exhibit B is nullified; client’s express walk-away condition is breached; confirmation findings on fairness and feasibility that rely on post-effective-date protections are undermined.

IV. RECONCILIATION MATRIX (MARKUP × SCHEDULES/EXHIBITS × CLIENT INSTRUCTION)

| # | Topic | Debtor Plan / Base | Committee Markup | Controlling Schedule/Exhibit | Client Instruction | Disposition |
|---|--------|--------------------|------------------|------------------------------|--------------------|-------------|
| 1a | Indemnification basket | Deductible basket | Tipping (first-dollar) basket | Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities | Concede basket conversion | ACCEPT WITH CONDITIONS (conform Schedule 5.2; no silent shift of retained liabilities) |
| 1b | Indemnification cap | Baseline cap | Silent reduction | Schedule 5.2; valuation summary | (Not conceded; protect economics) | REJECT silent reduction; restore/re-strike cap expressly |
| 2 | MAE – regulatory carve-outs | No such carve-outs | Carve-outs for regulatory action of the kind at issue | Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries) | Protect against known regulatory risk | REJECT; preserve MAE reach over Schedule 3.7-type risk |
| 3 | Survival / limitation | Exhibit B survival matrix | New shorter limitation period for core reps | Exhibit B survival matrix | Survival-period reduction = walk-away | REJECT; walk-away if Committee insists |

V. OTHER PLAN PROVISIONS

Aside from the three deviations above, the Committee Markup accepts most firm-standard and Debtor Plan provisions (including the general architecture of representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing/effectiveness, and termination mechanics not implicated by the MAE and survival edits). No additional operative deviations were identified in the counterparty markup record beyond the indemnification economics, MAE regulatory carve-outs, and survival limitation-period changes. Any clean-up conforming changes that merely implement an accepted disposition above should be cabined to those topics and should not reopen settled plan treatment, classification, or distribution mechanics.

VI. DISCLOSURE STATEMENT, VALUATION, AND CONFIRMATION IMPLICATIONS

1. Disclosure statement excerpts must be conformed to any accepted change in basket type and to the final cap, and must continue to describe Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries without suggesting that MAE or related conditions exclude them.
2. Valuation summary residual-value and indemnity-capacity assumptions must be refreshed if the cap is renegotiated; a silent cap cut is incompatible with an unchanged valuation narrative.
3. Exhibit B and Schedule 5.2 should be expressly reaffirmed or amended in the plan supplement package; silent inconsistency between redlined plan text and controlling schedules/exhibits is unacceptable for confirmation.
4. Feasibility, good-faith, and fairness presentations at confirmation should reflect the controlling client positions: tipping basket only with repaired cap and Schedule 5.2 alignment; no MAE regulatory carve-out for Schedule 3.7-type risk; full Exhibit B survival on core representations.

VII. RECOMMENDED RESPONSE PACKAGE TO THE COMMITTEE

1. Accept conversion of the indemnification basket from deductible to tipping, conditioned on:
   - restoration of the Debtor Plan indemnification cap (or an expressly negotiated substitute cap at not less than baseline economics);
   - conforming revisions to Schedule 5.2 / plan supplement retained-liability listings so tipping does not silently reallocate those items;
   - conspicuous redline and disclosure-statement/valuation conforming edits (no silent economics changes).
2. Reject MAE regulatory-action carve-outs; restore Debtor Plan MAE language or negotiate a formulation that preserves coverage for the Schedule 3.7 inquiries and materially similar regulatory action.
3. Reject the shortened survival / new limitation period for core representations as a walk-away item; reinstate the Exhibit B survival matrix without cross-cutting abbreviation.
4. Require a conformed plan supplement set (Schedule 3.7 affirmation, Schedule 5.2 alignment, Exhibit B restatement) before any further solicitation or confirmation briefing relies on the Redline.
5. Do not rely on superseded earlier partner-thread priorities; all negotiation authority tracks the latest instruction (basket convertible; survival reduction = walk-away).

VIII. CONCLUSION

The Committee Redline is largely constructive but contains three deviations that must be resolved against the Debtor Plan, the valuation summary, the disclosure statement excerpts, and—critically—the controlling schedules, exhibits, and client instruction. The basket conversion may be conceded on documented conditions. The silent cap reduction and the MAE regulatory carve-outs should be rejected and repaired. The survival-period reduction contradicts Exhibit B and is a client walk-away issue. Addressing every deviation on that basis will restore consistency among the plan text, Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, Exhibit B, the valuation summary, and the disclosure statement, and will place the case in a confirmation-ready posture consistent with the engagement instruction.

Respectfully submitted,
[Restructuring Team]

End of report.
